# Aftercare
## Monitor
- oxygenation, circulating blood, and perfusion; - pressure, cardiac rhythm, shock, and consciousness; - external and internal bleeding; - dressing saturation and contamination; - infection, necrosis, and scar state; - organ, bone, tendon, nerve, and joint function; - active drugs and toxic burden; - cyberware power, heat, EMP state, and neural link.
## After a dressing or hemostatic packing
1. Repeat analysis. 2. Check the new external bleeding rate. 3. Monitor dressing saturation. 4. Replace a saturated item or perform vascular repair.
## After a tourniquet
1. Record the installation time in character. 2. Monitor limb ischemia. 3. Prepare wound control equipment and blood before removal. 4. Remove the tourniquet. 5. Check for recurrent bleeding and distal region function.
## After transfusion
1. Repeat the blood and perfusion scan. 2. Check the compatibility response. 3. Confirm that active bleeding is controlled.
## After surgery
1. Check every surgical incision and open access path. 2. Check external and internal bleeding. 3. Check function of the operated organ or limb. 4. Check infection, contamination, and necrosis. 5. Check active drugs and toxic burden. 6. Repeat a full scan after the state updates.
## Patient handoff
Report the trauma mechanism and time, affected regions, active bleeding sources, tourniquet time, administered drugs, transfusions, performed interventions, installed transplant or cyberware, and remaining restrictions.
